text: Scharfenstein Castle, German name Burg Scharfenstein, is a ruined castle near the town of Kiedrich in Hesse, Germany, and was part of the Bishopric of Mainz's border fortifications.
Scharfenstein Castle was erected in 1160 under Christian I, Archbishop of Mainz, and it survives today as a ruin near the town of Kiedrich in Hesse, Germany.
Abergairn Castle is a ruined castle dating from the 17th century, located about one mile north of Ballater, Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
Abergairn Castle is built on the top of an isolated kame, at the north east of the entrance to Glen Gairn.
Chateau de Longwy is a ruined castle, incorporated into the town's fortifications, in the commune of Longwy in the Meurthe-et-Moselle department of France.
The ruined Chateau de Longwy is incorporated into the fortifications of the town of Longwy, a commune in the Meurthe-et-Moselle department of France.
Clun Castle is a ruined castle in the small town of Clun, Shropshire, established by the Norman lord Robert de Say after the Norman invasion of England.

Clun Castle became an important Marcher lord castle in the 12th century, with an extensive castle-guard system, and was owned for many years by the Fitzalan family, who used it to protect the region from Welsh attack.
The Fitzalans converted Clun Castle into a hunting lodge with pleasure gardens in the 14th century, but by the 16th century the castle was largely ruined.

Clun Castle was gradually abandoned as a property in favour of the more luxurious Arundel Castle, was slighted in 1646 after the English Civil War, and remained in poor condition until renovation work in the 1890s.
Inch Castle is a ruined castle located on the southern tip of Inch Island in County Donegal, Ireland, constructed around 1430.
Inch Castle was built by the Gaelic Irish lord Neachtain O'Donnell for his father-in-law Cahir O'Doherty.

The O'Dohertys were the dominant family on the nearby peninsula of Inishowen and had close links with the O'Donnells; Inch Castle formed part of their defensive network of fortifications against rival clans.

Castillo de Tabernas is a ruined castle on the outskirts of the municipality of Tabernas, Almeria province, in the autonomous community of Andalusia, Spain, built in the 11th century during Arab domination.
Castillo de Tabernas is of Moorish style and sits on top of a hill; when it was built it occupied the entire hill, though currently only a part is preserved.
Castillo de Tabernas was declared a Bien de Interes Cultural monument in 1993, and during the siege of Almeria, Ferdinand and Isabella ensconced themselves in the castle.
The Wegelnburg is a ruined castle near Schonau in the Palatinate Forest in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, near the border with France.
The Wegelnburg stands at a height of 572 m, making it the highest ruined castle in the Palatinate Forest.

Cairnburgh Castle is a ruined castle located on the islands of Cairn na Burgh Mor and Cairn na Burgh Beag, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, at the northern extremity of the Treshnish Isles at the mouth of Loch Tuath, north of Iona.
The 1991 book The Changing Scottish Landscape characterises Cairnburgh Castle as one of the most isolated fortifications in Britain and also one of the strangest.
Isabella Kelly, nee Fordyce, also known as Isabella Hedgeland, was a Scottish novelist and poet.
Isabella Kelly was born at Cairnburgh Castle in the Scottish Highlands, baptised on 4 May 1759, and died on 25 June 1857 in London.
Schauenberg is a hill and ruined castle near Turbenthal, canton of Zurich, at 892 m.

There were fortifications at Schauenberg since the Iron Age, and from the early 13th century a wooden structure stood there, extended in the 1250s to a massive keep; the fortress was destroyed in 1344.

From 1622 Zurich maintained a system of beacons as a warning system, and signals from Schauenberg could be seen at places including Schnabel (Albis), Pfannenstiel, Uetliberg, Zurichberg, Kyburg and Hohenklingen.

Naval Consolidated Brig, Miramar (NAVCONBRIG) is a military prison operated by the U.S. Navy at Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in Miramar, San Diego, California, just under 10 mi north of downtown San Diego.

NAVCONBRIG is one of three Navy consolidated brigs and the Pacific area regional confinement facility for the United States Department of Defense; it is also known as the Joint Regional Correctional Facility Southwest.
The 208000 sqft Naval Consolidated Brig, Miramar has a capacity of up to 400 male and/or female prisoners and is staffed with 31 civilian and 173 military personnel.
Music Instructor is a German electro-dance music project whose producers and songwriters are Mike Michaels, Mark "MM" Dollar, and Mark Tabak, also known as Triple-M Crew.
Triple-M has also produced other artists and bands such as Brainbug, Flying Steps, Mystica, Highland, The Boyz, Overground, Before Four, US5 and Ayman.
Music Instructor often worked with many other artists, especially a group called Lunatics and a breakdance crew called Flying Steps, and was most active in the late 1990s and early 2000s.
Naval Submarine Base New London is the United States Navy's primary East Coast submarine base, also known as the Home of the Submarine Force, and is located in Groton, Connecticut.
Naval Submarine Base New London, the Navy's primary East Coast submarine base, is located in Groton, Connecticut, and is known as the Home of the Submarine Force.
Lara Croft: Tomb Raider is a 2001 action-adventure film based on the Tomb Raider video game series, featuring the character Lara Croft portrayed by Angelina Jolie.

Lara Croft: Tomb Raider is an international co-production between the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, and Germany, directed by Simon West, and revolves around Lara Croft trying to obtain ancient artifacts from the Illuminati.
Royal Air Force Croft, or RAF Croft, is a former Royal Air Force station located 4.6 mi south of Darlington, County Durham, England and 8 mi north east of Richmond, North Yorkshire.
RAF Croft is also known locally as Croft Aerodrome or Neasham, and is a former Royal Air Force station located 4.6 mi south of Darlington, County Durham, England.
John Ellis Roosevelt Estate, also known as Meadow Croft, is a historic estate at Sayville in Suffolk County, New York.
The John Ellis Roosevelt Estate main house is roughly L-shaped, with an original farmhouse built about 1850 and a larger Colonial Revival mansion built 1891-1892 set perpendicular to it.
The property was purchased by Robert Barnwell Roosevelt (1829-1906) in 1873, and his son John Ellis Roosevelt (1853-1939) commissioned the estate.
Bibhu Prasad Tripathy is an Advocate, Solicitor and Writer with over one and a half decades of experience as a law practitioner.

Bibhu Prasad Tripathy has practised in the Supreme Court of India, Delhi High Court, Odisha High Court, National Consumer Forum and Environment Appellate Authority, and holds an LL.B from University of Delhi and an LL.M from the National Law School of India University, Bangalore.

Bibhu Prasad Tripathy is the standing counsel for the School and Mass Education Department, Government of Odisha, and wrote books including Legal Compendium for investigating officer of Women and Children Desk and Urban Police Act.
Robert Croft is a free-diver who, in 1967, became the first person to free-dive beyond the depth of 200 feet.

Robert Croft was a US Navy diving instructor in 1962 at the US Naval Submarine Base New London submarine school in Groton, Connecticut, where instructors trained prospective submariners to escape from a disabled submarine in the submarine escape training tank.

Tomb Raider, also known as Lara Croft: Tomb Raider between 2001 and 2007, is a media franchise that originated with an action-adventure video game series created by British gaming company Core Design.
The Tomb Raider franchise was formerly owned by Eidos Interactive, then by Square Enix after its acquisition of Eidos in 2009, and focuses on the fictional English archaeologist Lara Croft.

Additional Tomb Raider media has grown up around the theme in the form of film adaptations, comics and novels, while the games focus on action-adventure exploration, solving puzzles, navigating hostile environments filled with traps, and fighting numerous enemies.

Jack Baer (October 29, 1914 - March 9, 2002), son of Herman and Anna Baer, graduated from Shawnee (Oklahoma) High School in 1933 as an all-round athlete and was offered a contract with the New York Yankees but opted to play football and baseball at the University of Oklahoma.
Jack Baer was a quarterback at the University of Oklahoma who set records as a punter and kicker, was named All-Big Six, and at one point held the record for field goals after booting a 47 yarder.

Jack Baer was the fourth head baseball coach at the University of Oklahoma, beginning in 1942, and during his tenure Oklahoma won one national championship in 1951, made five NCAA Tournament appearances and won 6 conference titles; he retired in 1968 and is buried in the IOOF Cemetery in Norman, Oklahoma.
The Fly is a song by Irish rock band U2, the seventh track from their 1991 album Achtung Baby, released as the album's first single on 21 October 1991.

The Fly introduced a more abrasive sounding U2, featuring danceable hip-hop beats, industrial textures, distorted vocals, and an elaborate guitar solo; lead vocalist Bono described it as the sound of four men chopping down The Joshua Tree.
Win is a trilingual romance thriller film directed in Hindi, Telugu and Tamil by Vinod Kumar, who makes his first directorial debut; it was written by Vinod Kumar assisted by Sudarshanan.

The film Win is released under the banner of Rahmath Productions in Telugu and Jai Balaji Movie Makers in Tamil, and features Jai Akash alongside Angel Jitendra, Kavya, Nikita, Kousalya, Dinesh Nair, S. Ve. Sheker and Ganja Karuppu.

The background score and soundtrack of Win are composed by U. K. Murali, with the Telugu audio released on 28 March 2013, and three music directors, Shankar Ganesh, Deva and A. R. Reihana, sing a song together for the film.
Govinda Jaya Jaya is an Indian devotional chant or song, often sung in the Krishna Consciousness movement founded by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada and by Hindus in general.

Prabhupada's devotees at Radha Krishna Temple (London) recorded the chant as Govinda Jai Jai for their eponymous album, produced by George Harrison and released on the Beatles' Apple record label in 1971.
An edited version of the Radha Krishna Temple (London) recording was first issued as the B-side of the devotees' 1970 single Govinda.
U218 Singles is a greatest hits album by the Irish rock band U2, released in November 2006, containing 18 songs in most markets.

The seventeenth track on U218 Singles is a cover of The Skids' The Saints Are Coming, recorded in collaboration with Green Day to benefit Hurricane Katrina charities, and the closing eighteenth track is the new song Window in the Skies.
In some markets, such as the United Kingdom, I Will Follow is added as the opening track of U218 Singles, and the U218 Videos DVD featuring U2 music videos was released concurrently.

Jai Ho! (You Are My Destiny) is a song performed by American girl group The Pussycat Dolls for their second studio album Doll Domination (2008), released on February 23, 2009 by Interscope Records as the fourth single from the record.

After watching Slumdog Millionaire, record executives Jimmy Iovine and Ron Fair wanted to turn Jai Ho into a pop record without deviating from the original melody and asked Nicole Scherzinger to do her own interpretation of the song.
The song Jai Ho! (You Are My Destiny) was credited as A. R. Rahman and The Pussycat Dolls featuring Nicole Scherzinger.
Heartbeat is the first single from The Fray's third album Scars & Stories, and the band premiered the song while opening for U2 on their U2 360 Tour in May 2011.
Heartbeat was released for airplay on October 8, 2011, and for download in the United States on iTunes on October 11, 2011.
With or Without You is a song by Irish rock band U2, the third track from their fifth studio album The Joshua Tree (1987), released as the album's lead single on 16 March 1987.

With or Without You was the group's most successful single at the time, becoming their first number-one hit in both the United States and Canada by topping the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks and the RPM national singles chart for one week, with a further three weeks at number two.
Believe is the debut studio album by Scottish singer and Britain's Got Talent winner Jai McDowall, released on 9 December 2011 via Sony Music and Syco Music.
A promotional single from Jai McDowall's album Believe, titled With or Without You, was released and performed on various UK shows such as Daybreak.
Brothers of the Road is the eighth studio album, and tenth album overall, by the rock group the Allman Brothers Band, released in 1981.

Brothers of the Road is the Allman Brothers Band's only album without drummer Jai Johanny Johanson, the last album to feature bassist David Goldflies and guitarist Dan Toler, and the only album to feature drummer David Toler.
The song Straight from the Heart was the Allman Brothers Band's third, and to date last, Top 40 hit.
Bill Grainer is a Grammy certified American songwriter and producer who has written for artists including Jai McDowall, Linda Eder, and Jennifer Hudson.
Bill Grainer co-wrote the song Stand Up with Jennifer Hudson for her Grammy Award-winning self-titled debut album.
Rebecca Gayheart (born August 12, 1971) is an American fashion model and television and film actress who began her career appearing in a student short film by Brett Ratner.

Rebecca Gayheart gained notice as a spokesperson and model for Noxzema in the early 1990s, had minor roles in Nothing to Lose and Scream 2 (1997), and starred in the 1998 slasher film Urban Legend and the black comedy Jawbreaker (1999).
Rebecca Gayheart has had roles on the television series Dead Like Me, Vanished, and Nip/Tuck.
Scream 2 is the fifth studio album by German trance producer and DJ Markus Schulz, released on 21 February 2014 by Armada Music.
Markus Schulz is a German trance producer and DJ whose fifth studio album is titled Scream 2, the same title as the 1997 American slasher film directed by Wes Craven.

Timothy David Olyphant (born May 20, 1968) is an American actor and producer who made his Off-Broadway acting debut in 1995 in The Monogamist, winning the Theatre World Award, and originated David Sedaris' The Santaland Diaries in 1996.
In the early years of his career Timothy Olyphant was often cast in supporting villainous roles, most notably in Scream 2 (1997), Go (1999), A Man Apart (2003) and The Girl Next Door (2004).

Timothy Olyphant came to wider attention as Sheriff Seth Bullock in HBO's western Deadwood (2004-2006), then starred in Catch and Release (2006), Hitman (2007), A Perfect Getaway (2009) and The Crazies (2010), and was a villain in Live Free or Die Hard (2007).
Laura Elizabeth Laurie Metcalf (born June 16, 1955) is an American actress known for playing Jackie Harris on the ABC sitcom Roseanne (1988-97) and Mary Cooper on The Big Bang Theory (2007-present).

Laurie Metcalf also played Carolyn Bigsby on Desperate Housewives (2006), Dr. Jenna James on Getting On (2013-15), and Marjorie McCarthy in The McCarthys (2014-15), and voiced Mrs. Davis in the Toy Story film series.

Laurie Metcalf's other film appearances include Making Mr. Right (1987), JFK (1991), Mistress (1992), and Debbie Salt / Mrs. Loomis in Scream 2 (1997), and she has appeared in commercials for Plan USA.
Robert Bobby Gaylor, Jr. is an American writer, actor, voice actor, producer, director, spoken word artist and former stand-up comic who was raised in Boston.

Bobby Gaylor moved to L.A. to write for Roseanne Barr's television sitcom Roseanne, and later paired his comedy writing and life stories with music, releasing with Marc Bonilla and Michael Scott an album called Fuzzatonic Scream on Atlantic Records.
Sidney Prescott is a fictional character and the primary protagonist of the Scream series, created by Kevin Williamson and portrayed by Canadian actress Neve Campbell.
Sidney Prescott first appeared in Scream (1996), followed by three sequels: Scream 2 (1997), Scream 3 (2000) and Scream 4 (2011).

Sidney Prescott is the target of killers who adopt the Ghostface persona, a ghost mask and black cloak, and the Ghostface killers often murder people close to her and taunt her by phone before a final confrontation revealing the true killer.
Scream 2 is a 1997 American slasher film directed by Wes Craven and written by Kevin Williamson.
Scream 2 stars David Arquette, Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Jamie Kennedy, Laurie Metcalf, Jerry O'Connell, Jada Pinkett and Liev Schreiber.

Scream is an American horror franchise created by Kevin Williamson and Wes Craven, starring Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox, and David Arquette, which grossed over $604 million in worldwide box-office receipts across four motion pictures directed by Craven.

The first Scream film was released on December 20, 1996 and is currently the highest-grossing slasher film in the United States; Scream 2 was released on December 12, 1997, Scream 3 on February 4, 2000, and Scream 4 on April 15, 2011, eleven years after the previous film.
The Scream films follow Sidney Prescott and her war against murderers who adopt the guise of Ghostface, with support from town deputy Dewey Riley, reporter Gale Weathers, and film-geek Randy Meeks.
MTV launched a television spin-off of the Scream film series on June 30, 2015; the TV series follows different characters and new storylines which are not connected to the film series.
Gale Weathers is a fictional character of the Scream series, created by Kevin Williamson and portrayed by Friends star Courteney Cox.

Gale Weathers first appeared in Scream (1996), followed by three sequels: Scream 2 (1997), Scream 3 (2000) and Scream 4 (2011), and is an ambitious, strong-willed journalist and writer who is initially built up as an antagonist.
Gale Weathers ultimately joins forces with Sidney Prescott and Dewey Riley to investigate and stop the Ghostface murders.
Wes Craven's Scream series features a large cast of characters created primarily by Kevin Williamson, with contributions from Craven and Ehren Kruger.

The Scream series comprises four films, Scream (1996), Scream 2 (1997), Scream 3 (2000) and Scream 4 (2011), and focuses on Sidney Prescott, played by Neve Campbell, and a succession of murderers who adopt the Ghostface disguise.
Five Forty Aviation Ltd, trading as Fly540, is a low-cost airline based in Nairobi, Kenya, which commenced operations in 2006 and operates domestic and international passenger and freight services.
Fly540 had two subsidiary airlines, Fly540 Ghana (suspended in May 2014 and since sold) and Fly540 Angola (suspended in May 2014), but has since focused its business expansion plans on East Africa.
The National Convention Party (NCP) is a political party in Gambia that was the main opposition party between 1975 and 1994.
The National Convention Party was founded on 7 September 1975 at Busumbala by former vice-president Sheriff Mustapha Dibba, two weeks after his expulsion from the People's Progressive Party (PPP).

The National Convention Party initially welcomed the 1994 coup but was banned from participating in elections in August 1994; its candidate Sheriff Dibba came fourth at the presidential elections of 18 October 2001 with 3.77% of the popular vote.
Fastjet Airlines Limited (Tanzania), also known as Fastjet Tanzania, is a low-cost airline based in Dar es Salaam that operates flights under the fastjet brand in Tanzania.
Fastjet Tanzania was founded in 2011 as Fly540 Tanzania, and was rebranded as Fastjet Tanzania after the acquisition of Fly540 in 2012.
Fastjet Tanzania carried more than 350,000 passengers in its first year of operations and sold one million seats by December 2014.
Christian Brothers College (CBC, St. Kilda) was founded in 1878 and is a Roman Catholic independent secondary college for boys in the Melbourne suburb of St Kilda East.
Christian Brothers College is part of the Association of Edmund Rice schools; it was originally founded by the Christian Brothers, who are no longer involved in running the school.
The company was originally founded in Galt as the Dumfries Foundry in 1844 by James Andrews and James Crombie.
The Dumfries Foundry produced steam engines and also safe doors, though the exact number of products it manufactured during this period is unclear.
Genius (formerly Rap Genius) is a North American digital media company originally founded in August 2009 by Tom Lehman, Ilan Zechory, and Mahbod Moghadam.
Genius allows users to provide annotations and interpretation of song lyrics, news stories, sources, poetry, and documents.
Artillerie-Inrichtingen was a Dutch State-Owned artillery, small arms, and munitions company which also produced machine tools, originally founded in 1679 in Delft, Netherlands.
Artillerie-Inrichtingen was split in 1973, with its defense-related businesses becoming Eurometaal and its civilian manufacturing becoming Hembrug Machine Tools.
During its years as Artillerie-Inrichtingen, the company manufactured armaments and industrial outputs for the Dutch Army and the Royal Dutch East Indies Army (KNIL).
Teletrol (Teletrol Systems Inc.) is a United States company based in Manchester, New Hampshire, originally founded in 1981 as Teletrol, Inc.
Teletrol was acquired in 1985 by Philips, under which it continues to operate as a subsidiary, and is a supplier of building automation systems and components.

Teletrol's products centralise management and control of HVAC and lighting systems, using hardware thermostatic controllers installed at remote sites and browser-based software communicating over HTTP.
Totally Games was an electronic game developer located in Marin County, California, whose titles included the X-wing series based on Star Wars and Bridge Commander based on Star Trek.

Totally Games made PC-based World War II flight combat simulations Battlehawks 1942, Their Finest Hour, The Battle of Britain, and Secret Weapons of the Luftwaffe, and created Secret Weapons over Normandy in 2003 for the PS2, X-Box and PC.
Totally Games was founded in 1985 as a sole proprietorship, incorporated in 1993 as Peregrine Software, and soon renamed Totally Games by Lawrence Holland, a Cornell University graduate.

SemGroup is a transporter of oil and natural gas through pipelines from refineries to end users, an operator of oil terminals, and a manufacturer and seller of asphalt, headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
SemGroup began trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol SEMG in 2010, was originally founded in 2000, and as of 2007 was the 18th largest private company in the US.
SemGroup filed for bankruptcy in 2008 and as of December 2009 had restructured and emerged from bankruptcy at a reduced size.

Ines Reingold-Tali, known by the stage names Inez, Inèz or Inez, is an Estonian new media artist, musician, composer and writer on sound art, noise, electronic music, glitch and digital culture who lives and works in Finland.

Ines Reingold-Tali has been part of a new generation of Finnish composers since the mid-1990s, and her works have been published by labels including K-tel International, FG Music/Naxos, YOCOMA, YAP and Charm of Sound.

Ines Reingold-Tali was nominated for the Florence Biennale 2007 in Italy, received an award at the LACDA International Juried Competition Winners Show in 2007 at the Los Angeles Center for Digital Art, and was nominated for the 30e Festival International des Musiques Syntheses in France in 2000.
Sixtoo was the main project of Canadian underground hip hop DJ, producer and rapper Vaughn Robert Squire between 1996 and 2007.

Vaughn Robert Squire retired the Sixtoo name to pursue other directions in electronic music, shifting from experimental hip hop to deeper club sounds of various tempos; he is also known as C.L. S.C.A.R.R., Speakerbruiser Rob, and Prison Garde.
This is a list of sound artists; sound art is a diverse group of art practices whose predominant focus is wide notions of sound, listening and hearing.

There is contention over which artists count as sound artists, or whether another category such as experimental music, electronic music, sound installation, circuit bending, noise music, acoustic ecology, sound poetry or Fluxus might be more accurate.

Beautiful Eulogy is a Christian experimental hip hop group and production team from Portland, Oregon, signed to the label Humble Beast, composed of rappers Braille and Odd Thomas and producer Courtland Urbano.

Beautiful Eulogy coalesced in 2011 while Braille, Odd Thomas and Courtland Urbano were creating Braille's seventh release, Native Lungs, and the group blends hip hop with folk, electronic, hymn tunes and modern worship music.

Beautiful Eulogy released its debut album Satellite Kite on June 19, 2012, and its second album Instruments of Mercy on October 29, 2013; after contributing to the charity compilation King Kulture and guesting on Lecrae's Church Clothes, the group earned critical acclaim.
Experimental hip hop, also known as abstract hip hop, is a genre of hip hop that employs structural elements typically considered unconventional in traditional hip hop music.

Notable experimental hip hop record labels include Definitive Jux, Anticon, Big Dada and Ninja Tune, and while most experimental hip hop incorporates turntablism and is produced electronically, some artists have introduced acoustic elements to perform it live.

Hip hop is a subculture and art movement developed in the South Bronx in New York City during the late 1970s, and is characterised by nine distinct elements or expressive realms, of which hip hop music (rapping, djaying, beatboxing and breaking) is only four.

Afrika Bambaataa of the hip hop collective Zulu Nation outlined the pillars of hip hop culture: rapping (also called MCing or emceeing), DJing (and turntablism), b-boying/b-girling/breakdancing, and graffiti art, which he called aerosol writin'.
Cyclic Defrost is an Australian specialist electronic music magazine founded and edited by Sebastian Chan, with current editors Bob Baker Fish, Chris Downton and Peter Hollo.
Cyclic Defrost covers independent electronic music, avant-rock, experimental sound art and left field hip hop.
Petri Kuljuntausta is a Finnish composer, musician, sound artist and author of three books on electronic music and sound art.
Petri Kuljuntausta has belonged to a new generation of composers in Finland interested in experimental and electronic music since the 1990s.
and/OAR is an independent record label based in Seattle, Washington, USA, founded by Dale Lloyd in 2001 and officially launched in May 2002.

and/OAR focuses on field recordings and experimental sound art that utilises field recording as part of the creative process, released field recording compilations for Phonography.org from 2001 to 2005, and had issued over 70 releases on CD and CD-R as of December 2014.
and/OAR offered free MP3 releases through its website from 2008 to 2010, a format since discontinued.
Lloyd John Dunn (born November 10, 1957 in Harlan, Iowa, USA) is a founding member of the mixed-media and experimental sound art group the Tape-beatles.

Lloyd John Dunn founded, published and edited several small-press magazines, including PhotoStatic and Retrofuturism, and since the early 1980s has made work for film, video, audio, print, and the web.
The George H. Williams Townhouses, commonly known as The Lawn apartments, in northwest Portland, Oregon, are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The three-unit townhouse structure was built for and originally owned by George Henry Williams, a former United States Attorney General, United States Senator for Oregon, Oregon Supreme Court Chief Justice and later mayor of Portland, as a business investment he did not reside in.
The George H. Williams Townhouses were moved in 1922, from the northwest corner of the block at the southeast corner of NW 19th and Davis to the corner at NW 18th and Davis.
Buchanan Township is one of eleven townships in Atchison County, Missouri, United States, and had a population of 83 at the 2010 census.
The northwest corner of Buchanan Township is the northwest corner of the entire state of Missouri.
Dade County is a county in the U.S. state of Georgia that occupies the northwest corner of Georgia; its own northwest corner is the westernmost point in the state.
Dade County had a population of 16,633 at the 2010 census, and its county seat and only incorporated municipality is Trenton.

Franklin Street Presbyterian Church and Parsonage is a historic Presbyterian church at 100 West Franklin Street, at Cathedral Street, in Baltimore, Maryland; a rectangular Tudor Gothic building dedicated in 1847, with an addition in 1865, and a parsonage built in 1857.

The Franklin Street Presbyterian Church was incorporated in 1844 by men from the First Presbyterian Church, and in 1973 the two congregations reunited to form The First and Franklin Street Presbyterian Church, centred at the First Church site on West Madison and Park.

The Franklin Street building was later sold to a fundamentalist independent Protestant congregation and re-sold to the present New Unity Church Ministries; the Maryland Club, founded 1857, once occupied a Greek Revival home across Cathedral Street designed by Robert Mills.
Nelson is a town in Cheshire County, New Hampshire, United States, with a population of 729 at the 2010 census, and includes the village of Munsonville.
The town of Nelson, New Hampshire, includes the village of Munsonville, so Munsonville is part of the town of Nelson in Cheshire County.
Bennetts Bayou is a stream in the U.S. states of Arkansas and Missouri, whose source is in Howell County, Missouri, just south of US Route 160 west of Hocomo.

Bennetts Bayou flows southwest into Ozark County, Missouri, then south through the northwest corner of Fulton County, Arkansas and into Baxter County, Arkansas, and enters the northeast arm of Norfork Lake east of Gamaliel, Arkansas; the similarly named Bennetts River runs subparallel just to the southeast.

Lobster Lake in the North Maine Woods was named because its shape resembles the outline of a lobster, with a curled tail-like northwest corner in Northeast Carry township and an eastward arm in Lobster township resembling a thorax.

Lobster Lake's larger southward eastern arm is called Big Claw and its smaller western arm is called Little Claw; Lobster Stream connects the lake's northwest corner to the West Branch Penobscot River 1.4 mi north of the lake.
Lobster Lake has self-sustaining populations of native lake trout and land-locked Atlantic salmon, but brook trout populations are suppressed by competition from yellow perch and white perch.
Sullivan's Corner Historic District is an 18 acre historic district at a rural crossroads in northeastern Norfolk, Massachusetts, including Norfolk's oldest cemetery, established c. 1736.

The Sullivan's Corner district includes five 18th- to early 20th-century buildings used as residences, four of which face the cemetery across Seekonk Street, and 1 Needham Street, one of Norfolk's best-preserved Greek Revival buildings.
Sullivan's Store in the Sullivan's Corner district was built c. 1913 and is Norfolk's only commercial building from that period, now converted to residential use.
Fairhope is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in Washington Township, Fayette County, Pennsylvania, United States, in the northwest corner of Fayette County.
Fairhope is bordered by Lynwood to the northwest, Naomi to the west, and Arnold City to the east; Pennsylvania Route 201 passes through it, and its population was 1,151 at the 2010 census.
Munsonville is an unincorporated community in the town of Nelson in Cheshire County, New Hampshire, located in the northwestern corner of Nelson around the outlet of Granite Lake.
Munsonville is a village within the town of Nelson, Cheshire County, New Hampshire, and its location is the northwestern corner of Nelson, around the outlet of Granite Lake.

Wild Mountain Thyme, also known as Purple Heather and Will Ye Go, Lassie, Go?, is a Scottish folk song collected by Francis McPeake 1st, who wrote the song himself for his wife; the McPeake family claims recognition for its writing.

The lyrics and melody of Wild Mountain Thyme are a variant of The Braes of Balquhither by Scottish poet Robert Tannahill (1774-1810), a contemporary of Robert Burns, first published in Robert Archibald Smith's Scottish Minstrel (1821-24).
A Pair of Brown Eyes is a single by The Pogues, released on 18 March 1985, which was their first to make the UK Top 100, peaking at Number 72.
A Pair of Brown Eyes was composed by Pogues front man Shane MacGowan on the melody of Wild Mountain Thyme, and featured on the band's second album Rum Sodomy & the Lash.
Bakhmull is an Aboriginal Afghan Hound, a long haired variety of the bakhmull tazi, an ancient group of oriental sighthounds that the Afghan Royal Family were the only humans to possess.

The bakhmull's coat is always fawn, ivory or white with a darker saddle, and red, red with white spots, black and black with white spots are not permissible colours; the breed hunts wild ram, ibex, hare, fox, wolf and jackal, and guards homes and flocks.

Since the 1980s the centre of Bakhmull breeding has been in Russia, at The Blue Dale el Bark Bakhmull in Moscow, and the breed standard was adopted in Moscow first in 1985 and later in 1997 (RFOS-RKF).
The album includes covers of Bob Dylan's Sweetheart Like You and The Blue Nile's The Downtown Lights, and a tribute song Muddy, Sam, And Otis to Muddy Waters, Sam Cooke, and Otis Redding.

Track 12 of the album, later released as a single featuring the Scottish Euro '96 Football Squad, is Purple Heather, a folk song normally called Wild Mountain Thyme, which is often credited as traditional but was written by The McPeakes.
Leave Virginia Alone was written by Tom Petty for his album Wildflowers, but was left off the finished album and given to Stewart instead.

American country artist Crystal Gayle has released fifteen music videos and sixty-eight singles, including six promotional singles, three singles as a collaborative artist, and five singles as a featured artist.

Crystal Gayle's debut single was the 1970 I've Cried (The Blue Right Out of My Eyes) via Decca Records, which reached the top forty of the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart; she then signed with United Artists Records, encouraged by her sister, to record country pop material.

Crystal Gayle's 1977 release Don't It Make My Brown Eyes Blue became her signature song, topping the country songs chart, reaching number two on the Billboard Hot 100, and bringing her crossover pop success.

After Don't It Make My Brown Eyes Blue, Crystal Gayle had three more number one country singles: Ready for the Times to Get Better, Why Have You Left the One You Left Me For, and the top-twenty pop hit Talking in Your Sleep.
Brown Eyes is a South Korean male duo consisting of members Yoon Gun and Naul, who released their first album, Brown Eyes, on June 7, 2001.
The South Korean male duo Brown Eyes, whose members are Yoon Gun and Naul, is written in Korean as 브라운아이즈.
Brown Eyes is a song by Fleetwood Mac from the 1979 double LP Tusk, one of six songs written and sung by Christine McVie.

Original Fleetwood Mac guitarist Peter Green took part in the sessions for Brown Eyes, but his playing is not credited, and in 1999 Green admitted he had no recollection of this contribution due to his deteriorating health in the 70s.
Brown Eyes was also performed by Fleetwood Mac on the Mirage Tour and the Shakin the Cage tour.
The Long Island Rugged Maniac 5K Obstacle Course event has been held annually in Wild Mountain since 2013, and currently takes place at the Wild Mountain Ski Area.
The Wild Mountain Ski Area is the venue where the Long Island Rugged Maniac 5K Obstacle Course event currently takes place, having hosted it annually since 2013.

Caramel is the second single from American R&B/hip hop trio City High's self-titled debut album in 2001, and was written based on the appearance and personality of Brian Gough, who is actually 5'6" with brown eyes rather than 5'5".
Caramel is City High's second most successful single, peaking at number 18 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number nine on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks in the U.S. in January 2002.
Beautiful Brown Eyes is a traditional country song arranged by Fiddlin' Arthur Smith and Alton Delmore of The Delmore Brothers in 1951.
An award was presented to Alton Delmore of The Delmore Brothers in 1951 for Beautiful Brown Eyes, the traditional country song that he and Fiddlin' Arthur Smith arranged.

Kurt Vonnegut Jr. (November 11, 1922 - April 11, 2007) was an American writer who published 14 novels, three short story collections, five plays, and five works of non-fiction over a career spanning over 50 years.
Kurt Vonnegut Jr. is most famous for his darkly satirical, best-selling novel Slaughterhouse-Five (1969), and was an American writer whose career spanned over 50 years.
